basis: Visual estimate from meadow-a-adventurous.png against meadow-a-2045.png. GCHQ's surveyed ring and aperture in the plate remain authoritative.

roofMix.reading: The ring roof is the dominant wildflower meadow, crossed by concentric mown walks. PV belongs mainly to the car-park canopies. Existing suburban roofs remain conventional.

wallMaterials.material: warm vertical timber or bronze fins
pale buff concrete or stone annexes

windowRhythm.storeyHeightMetres: 3.3 to 3.5 on the ring; annexes read as one tall industrial or civic storey
windowRhythm.windowWidthMetres: 2.0 to 2.8 glazing between narrow vertical fins
windowRhythm.windowProportion: About 0.65 to 0.85 width:height for each ring bay, combined into a continuous glazed band
windowRhythm.revealDepthImpression: Medium to strong, 250 to 400 mm behind a vertical fin line and roof edge.
windowRhythm.rhythm: Fine regular vertical bays around the curve, with continuous dark glazing. Annex walls are deliberately calm and almost blank.

groundCover.hardLandscapeColour: #77766F worn car-park asphalt and #A79A82 buff pedestrian routes
groundCover.reading: Parking remains extensive but is broken by solar canopies, tree avenues and planted edges. The central ring courtyard is dry planted ground, never water.

water.visible: Only small drainage and planted retention glints at car-park edges. The ring courtyard is dry and the roof aperture is not a pond.
water.pondSize: No major pond in the focal area
water.reflectivity: Small silver-blue fragments, #8FA6AA lit and #314B4E shaded, with reeds and tree shadow dominating.
water.buildability: Do not enlarge or relocate water to imitate the board's incidental glints. The meadow roof and canopies carry this view.

trees.density: Medium around the ring and high in perimeter belts. Car parks retain open visibility below the canopies.
trees.arrangement: Long avenues at car-park edges, irregular clumps around annexes, mature woodland beyond, and several trees in the dry inner courtyard.

sustainableFeatures.PVGlint: Carport roofs are blue-black #17232C with restrained edge glints #8C9FA7. Cars and asphalt must remain visible between rows.
sustainableFeatures.canopies: The defining secondary feature. Slender paired or single rows over all usable GCHQ parking, about 3.2 to 3.8 m underside height and roughly 40 per cent parking coverage.
sustainableFeatures.agrivoltaicRows: Not part of this focal scene.
sustainableFeatures.glasshouses: Not visible and should not be added.
sustainableFeatures.other: The 3.6 ha ring is a botanically varied meadow with two concentric mown routes, radial access cuts, darker outer planting and tiny walkers.

people/vehicles.people: Sparse walkers on roof paths, at the main entrance and between annexes. Roof figures are especially useful for proving the meadow is walkable.
people/vehicles.vehicles: Orderly parked cars remain visible beneath solar canopies, plus occasional moving vehicles on the perimeter road.
people/vehicles.scopeNote: The aerial plan currently omits people and cars. Existing photographed cars may remain under tile mode; new low-detail instances are optional only if canopy scale is unclear.

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate meadow roof is a flat olive disc with fine yellow speckle; the board has deep, varied late-summer planting, clear paths and a darker planted edge.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Increase multi-scale meadow variation, strengthen both concentric mown paths and radial cuts, and separate the edge planting by value rather than extra geometry.
gapsVsPlate.system: GCHQ roof shader in future.js and roof grade

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate carports are dark repeated slats that merge into the asphalt; board canopies read as elevated photovoltaic planes with cars, posts and gaps below.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Lift canopy readability with a lighter underside, explicit slim posts, accurate terrain-following heights and restrained PV glint. Preserve about 41 per cent parking coverage rather than filling every gap.
gapsVsPlate.system: canopy geometry in scripts/golden_valley_2045.py and futureGeometry in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate ring facade is a smooth blue-grey cylinder; the board has fine vertical timber or bronze bays and reflective glazing.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Add a curved facade material with regular vertical fins, a dark glazed band and a grounded plinth while preserving the exact surveyed ring outline and aperture.
gapsVsPlate.system: GCHQ model and facade materials in models.js or a dedicated material branch

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate trees are small angular repeats and leave the parking landscape exposed; board trees form mature avenues and dense perimeter masses.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Use taller avenue trees at measured edges, broaden veteran crowns and deepen canopy shadow. Keep clear sightlines to the ring.
gapsVsPlate.system: tree geometry/grade in landcover.js and future.js, plus gv-2045 tree data

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate asphalt and lawns are flat and dark; the board separates worn parking, buff walks, meadow verges and planted islands.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Separate parking from pedestrian hardscape in colour and roughness, soften verge edges and add broad low-frequency wear variation.
gapsVsPlate.system: gv-2045 land-cover data and ground shader in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board has visible cars and roof walkers; the plate has almost no scale cues.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Defer detailed people. If needed at M7, add a few roof sprites and ensure photographed or instanced cars remain readable under the canopies.
gapsVsPlate.system: optional life.js extension and tile visibility checks

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board subtly changes the ring profile, annex forms and surrounding town despite the geometry lock.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Do not reproduce those changes. The plate's GCHQ outline, aperture, annex positions and camera are the hard constraints.
